pretreatments.description: Hydrothermal pretreatment with four distinct temperatures set at 125 °C, 150 °C, 175 °C, and 200 °C were applied to Miscanthus. The procedure involved adding 2.5 g of Miscanthus and 25 mL of distilled water into a 100 mL stainless steel reactor, which was then placed in a high temperature rotation chamber for continuous mixing at 20 rpm. The reactors were maintained for 30 minutes, after which the temperature was set to the specific range (125-200 °C), and the system was allowed to cool. After the pretreatment period, the slurry was filtered for solid-liquid separation, and the recovered Miscanthus was washed with distilled water; however, washing is excluded per exclusion criteria for storage/preparation steps and freezing for storage, and the focus is on the hydrothermal condition which is classified as the pretreatment type. The process was followed by vacuum bagging for storage. The temperature variations (125 to 200 °C) reflect the condition variations of the same pretreatment method in different batches.
